entries.reason: The N stair tower houses the N range's stair: S_n climbs inside it and its treads meet the tower's walls
S_ne2 lands on the NE wall walk: its top tread is laid into the walk's edge
The stone flights up to the N rampart (T_n) land on its edge: their top treads are laid into the cornice
The curtains bond into the gatehouses (joined: castle-kit draws each face once); their copings run into the gate's masonry
The SE gatehouse's flank stones bond into the curtains either side of it
The SW drawbridge's chains and pulleys run into their slots in the gatehouse's face, the leaf's hinge irons into its threshold
The hourd's oak brackets are socketed into the gatehouse's face (putlog holes), as built
The SE bridge's last posts stand in the gate's threshold: the bridge abuts the gatehouse
The steward's house and its round stair turret are one building: the house's E gable framing runs into the turret
The AT gun's trail spades rest against the half-ring's sandbags
The telegraph wires are tied on the poles' insulators
A D tower's straight flanks are bonded into the curtain it flanks: they rise through the walk's outer edge to the tower's back wall
The SW curtain's walk runs onto the gatehouse's walk at one level where they bond (one floor, the joint under the gate's crown)
